 Slow-moving storm could bring heavy rain and slushy snow to the Plains as it pushes north
 Western South Dakota, western Nebraska, eastern Wyoming and parts of central North Dakota could see 1 to 3 inches of rain.
 By
 Hayley Vawter

 02:01 Heavy rain and slushy snow to slam the Plains as storm treks north 
 A storm system moving north out of the central Rockies and High Plains will bring rain to the Northern Plains as a strong area of high pressure over central and eastern Canada slows its progress. The stalled pattern could keep rain and even snow over parts of the western Dakotas and surrounding areas for an extended period.
 THE TAKEAWAY 
 A slow-moving storm could dump 1 to 3 inches of rain across parts of the Northern Plains.
 Colder air could turn rain to wet snow, with a few slushy inches possible above 5,000 to 5,500 feet.
 Rain could briefly mix with snow, but warm ground temperatures should prevent significant accumulation.
 A slow-moving storm is set to bring several days of rain and even some snow to parts of the Northern Plains.
 The storm will move north out of the central Rockies and High Plains, but a strong area of high pressure over Canada will prevent it from moving away quickly.

 That will allow rain to linger across parts of the Dakotas and surrounding states while colder air moves into the region, according to the FOX Forecast Center .
 Western South Dakota , western Nebraska , eastern Wyoming and parts of central North Dakota could see 1 to 3 inches of rain.

 As colder air arrives, some of that rain could change to wet snow in the higher elevations of South Dakota's Black Hills.
 A few inches of wet, slushy snow could accumulate above about 5,000 to 5,500 feet, mainly on grassy areas and higher terrain, the FOX Forecast Center said.

 Around Rapid City and the nearby foothills, rain could briefly mix with wet snow. However, temperatures near the ground should remain warm enough to prevent much snow from sticking.
 Roads could become wet or briefly slushy, but significant accumulation is not expected.

  Farther south, some rain could linger across West Texas as the storm pulls away. However, the Northern Plains will be the main area to watch Monday.
 A Level 1 out of 4 flash flood threat remains in West Texas.
